summary: Iteration 2 verification complete. All 4 requested features work: (1) server.py modularization — 38/38 iteration-1 regression tests still pass, (2) Resend emailer — welcome + booking-confirmation + password-reset emails logged with 'email:mock' subject/to lines (EMERGENT_EMAIL_KEY intentionally empty), (3) Emergent object storage — POST /api/upload + GET /api/files/{id} work with proper MIME/size validation and correct image/png Content-Type on download, (4) debounced live search on /services filters cards after ~350ms without pressing Enter. Booking wizard's new file-upload UI (images-file-input, images-file-label, remove-image-{i}) fully functional: file → upload → thumbnail → optional remove → booking created with images array containing /api/files/... URL. Full pytest run: 18/18 iteration-2 tests + 38/38 iteration-1 regression = 56/56 pass.
critical_code_review_comments: uploads.py imports 'new_id' and 'now_iso' from ..db but only uses 'now_iso' — 'new_id' is unused (nit).

uploads.py get /files/{id} accepts optional auth via header/query but silently allows anonymous reads if no token provided. That's an intentional 'public read' design (comment says so). Fine for image thumbnails, but any user who knows a file_id can read another user's uploaded image (uploaded images are not per-user gated). Consider tighter access control if user privacy for uploaded photos matters.

storage.py uses synchronous 'requests' inside an async FastAPI endpoint (put_object/get_object called from an async POST /upload). This blocks the event loop on network I/O. Consider httpx.AsyncClient for consistency (works today, but poor concurrency under load).
emailer.py send_email is async and uses httpx.AsyncClient — good. It never raises (fire-and-forget) — correct pattern.
auth.py forgot-password returns { ok:true, reset_token } — dev/demo convenience only; MUST be removed before prod (token leak). Comment already flags this.
server.py is now ~60 lines (was 1077) — modularization done cleanly. Each router file is well-scoped and reasonably sized (bookings/admin are the largest — still under 700 lines).
CORS still uses allow_origin_regex='.*' with allow_credentials=True — permissive for preview; tighten for prod.
In BookService.jsx handleFiles uploads files sequentially in a for-loop with await. For UX, parallel Promise.all() would be faster when picking multiple images.
